text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London reversed an early uptrend to end broadly lower, following steep losses in New York. July lost $65 to close at $1,825 per tonne, while September gave up $75 to close at $1,850 per tonne.

Brazil was again the main factor behind the wild swing with every hint of cold or warm weather used to push prices up or down. Arabica futures in New York tumbled nearly 14 per cent as weather forecasts calling for milder temperatures in Brazil and a bearish technical outlook sparked panicky speculative selling. The July/September spread showed a sharp decline today which is not a positive indication for the market.

Traders said that the wide swings occur against the background of unchanged fundamentals which makes it hard to predict future price moves. July lost a massive 35.35 cents/lb to close at 217.95 cents/lb, while September lost 26.85 cents/lb to close at 196.75 cents/lb.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell by 213 bags on June 9 to 44,002 60-kg bags, down from 44,215 bags on June 6 and 43,625 bags on June 5. On June 9, there were 250 bags pending grading in New York, 1,250 bags in New Orleans and 5,500 bags in Miami.

NORWAY - Norway imported 97,835 bags of coffee in April 1997, nearly 63 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 288,600 bags, 4.5 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by nearly 9 per cent to 719,900 bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/April 1997 were Guatemala (40,200 vs 31,100 bags), Mexico (35,700 vs 36,900 bags), Brazil (89,100 vs 66,400 bags) and Colombia (48,900 vs 50,900 bags).

SLOVAKIA - Slovakia imported 22,700 bags of coffee in March 1997, down from 26,800 bags imported the previous month. That brought total imports in the first quarter of 1997 up to 67,200 bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1997 were Honduras (10,800 bags) and India (10,000 bags).
